newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine neutral on Gazprom debt trading.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine neutral on Gazprom debt trading.

text.p: A Ukrainian deputy finance minister said on Thursday that Kiev had no strong feelings either way on a Russian bank's plan to issue international depositary receipts for Ukrainian debt to Russia's RAO Gazprom.

Under an agreement reached two years ago Ukraine's $1.4 billion gas debt was restructured for 12 years, Ukraine released bonds on the debt and transferred them to Gazprom, and Gazprom in turn passed $900 million of the debt to Russia's National Reserve Bank (NRB).
NRB president Alexandr Lebedev recently said his bank needed Ukraine's permission to trade the debt on the secondary market.
But the Ukrainian minister said it did not concern Kiev.
"We released these bonds, we are servicing the debt, we don't owe anything for it, and we will continue to work this way," Mykhailo Honcharuk said at a news conference.
"This is no longer Ukrainian property, and it is a matter for the Russian side on what to do with it," Honcharuk said.
Sources close to the matter said JP Morgan was working with the NRB to issue the international depositary receipts.
Ukraine is due to start paying the principal on the debt this year for a 10-year period.
